title: Refining the booking service
idea: Refinement means improving a working design in small, tested steps: clearer classes first, then faster code where a measurement shows a real cost.
points: Fix review findings and naming before you touch performance.
Optimise only a path you have measured or can count, like overlap checks.
Hide the change behind an existing class so callers stay untouched.
Re-run every test after each step, then write down the trade-off.

items.label: Measure
items.text: Count the work: each overlap check scans every booking for the room.

items.label: Pick one
items.text: Choose the single hottest spot. Leave the rest of the design alone.

items.label: Change inside
items.text: Sort bookings by start inside the repository. The service API stays the same.

items.label: Re-test
items.text: Run the boundary tests again: back-to-back, overlap, reversed slot.

items.label: Record
items.text: Write the trade-off down: faster checks, but the index assumes saved bookings never overlap.

code.title: Scan versus sorted lookup
code.caption: One room, fully booked in half-hour slots. Both stores answer the same question; count how many bookings each one examines. Think of both classes as two versions of the inside of `BookingRepository`: the service calls the same method either way.

walk.text: Sixteen back-to-back bookings go into both stores.
Before: a list scan that compares the slot with bookings one by one.
After: a `TreeMap` keyed by start time keeps bookings sorted.
Two lookups find the neighbours; each walks the tree in O(log n) steps, not every booking.
Overlap if the earlier one runs past our start, or the next begins before our end.

pitfalls: Do not optimise before tests exist; you cannot prove the faster code is still right.
The neighbour check assumes stored bookings never overlap; a policy allowing overlaps breaks it.
Two bookings with the same start overwrite each other in one `TreeMap` key.

quiz.why: `floorEntry` finds the 15.0 booking, which ends at 15.5, past 15.25. The tree looks at exactly two neighbours.

takeaway: Refine in small tested steps, and optimise only what you measured.

starters: How would I keep the TreeMap index safe with a ConflictPolicy?
Is the list scan ever good enough for a real office?
